ing: cut into large pieces on the bone
st: Cut the cabbage into wedges about 2 inches thick and cut the lamb into big chunks, leaving the bones in.
Put a layer of lamb in a large heavy pot and sprinkle with some of the flour, salt and a few peppercorns.
Add a layer of cabbage wedges and repeat the layers until everything is used, finishing with cabbage.
Pour in the [[2 cups]] water, cover and bring to a gentle boil over medium heat.
Lower the heat and simmer very gently for 2 hours, without stirring, until the lamb is falling off the bone.
Check the lamb is tender and well past 145°F (63°C). Add a splash of water if the pot is dry.
Gently stir once, tasting the broth, and add more salt if needed.
Serve hot in deep plates with boiled potatoes on the side. Warn guests about the whole peppercorns.
Put the potatoes in a pot with water and [[0.5 tsp]] salt. Boil for 20 minutes until tender, then keep warm.
In a bowl, mix the beef, onion, [[0.5 cup]] milk, [[2 tbsp]] flour, nutmeg, ginger, [[0.5 tsp]] salt and the pepper.
Mix well with your hands for 2 minutes until sticky and smooth. Chill for 10 minutes.
Wet your hands and shape the meat into 8 flat oval patties.
Melt [[1.5 tbsp]] butter in a large skillet over medium heat. Brown the patties for 4 minutes per side.
Move the patties to a plate. They should reach 160°F (71°C) inside.
In the same skillet, melt [[1.5 tbsp]] butter, whisk in [[3 tbsp]] flour and cook for 1 minute.
Slowly whisk in the broth and [[1 cup]] milk and simmer for 5 minutes into a smooth brown gravy. Season with [[0.5 tsp]] salt.
Return the patties to the gravy and simmer for 5 minutes. Serve with the potatoes and lingonberry jam.
Soak the salted lamb or ham hock in cold water overnight, changing the water once, to remove the extra salt.
Put the drained meat in a large pot with [[10 cups]] fresh water. Bring to a boil, skim, then simmer for 1 hour.
Squeeze the grated raw potatoes in a clean towel to remove as much liquid as you can.
Mix the grated and mashed potatoes with the flour and [[1 tsp]] salt into a thick sticky dough. Cook a small test dumpling in the simmering broth and adjust with flour if it falls apart.
Add the rutabaga and carrots to the pot and cook for 10 minutes.
With wet hands, shape the dough into 12 balls, a bit bigger than a golf ball.
Drop the dumplings into the simmering broth, cover and cook gently for 40 minutes without stirring hard.
Meanwhile, fry the bacon in a skillet until crisp.
Lift out the dumplings, vegetables and meat. Serve with the bacon, melted butter and a ladle of broth.
Buy ready-to-cook lutefisk that has been soaked in fresh water to remove the lye. Rinse it under cold water for several minutes and check it with a clean finger for any slippery lye feel.
Heat the oven to 400°F (200°C). Put the fish skin-side down in a baking dish, sprinkle with [[1 tsp]] salt and cover tightly with foil.
Bake for 20 to 30 minutes until the fish is opaque and flakes easily.
Boil the potatoes in water with [[0.5 tsp]] salt for 20 minutes until tender.
Heat the peas with a splash of water and [[0.5 tsp]] salt, mashing lightly if you want them thick.
Fry the bacon in a skillet until crisp and keep the bits and the fat.
Drain off any liquid that has collected around the baked fish.
Serve the fish with the potatoes, peas, bacon and melted butter, and add white pepper.

ing: skin on, very fresh or previously frozen, pin bones removed
st: Use salmon labeled safe for raw eating, or freeze it at 0°F (-18°C) for at least 7 days first. Thaw in the fridge.
Mix the salt, sugar and crushed pepper in a bowl.
Cut the salmon in two equal halves. Lay one half skin-side down in a dish and cover with half of the dill.
Pack the salt mixture evenly over the flesh, then add the rest of the dill.
Place the other half on top, flesh-side down, to form a sandwich.
Wrap tightly in plastic, set a plate with a weight such as a can on top, and refrigerate.
Cure for 48 hours, turning the package over every 12 hours and spooning the liquid over the fish. The total cure is long, so start two days ahead.
Scrape off the dill and salt and pat dry. Slice thinly on an angle away from the skin.
Whisk the Dijon, honey and oil into a sauce, stir in a little chopped dill, and serve with the salmon.

ing: cod or haddock, cut into chunks
st: Melt the butter in a large pot over medium heat and cook the leek for 3 minutes until soft.
Stir in the flour and cook for 1 minute.
Slowly pour in the fish stock while whisking so there are no lumps.
Add the carrots and potatoes and simmer for 12 to 15 minutes until almost tender.
Pour in the cream and bring back to a gentle simmer.
Add the fish and salmon chunks and poach gently for 4 to 5 minutes until opaque (145°F/63°C).
Season with salt and white pepper without stirring too hard so the fish stays in pieces.
Ladle into bowls and sprinkle with chives. Serve with bread.
Boil the potatoes in salted water for 20 minutes until very tender, then drain.
Put the potatoes through a ricer or mash until completely smooth with no lumps.
Mix in the butter, cream, sugar and salt, and spread on a tray. Cool completely in the fridge, about 1 hour.
Mix [[1.25 cups]] flour into the cold potatoes to form a soft dough.
Divide the dough into 8 balls. Work with one at a time on a well-floured surface.
Roll each ball paper-thin, about 10 inches wide, with a lot of flour on the board and pin.
Heat a dry skillet or griddle over medium-high heat. Cook each round for about 1 minute per side until pale with light brown spots.
Stack the cooked lefse between damp towels so they stay soft.
Serve warm with butter and sugar, folded into quarters.

ing: birch twigs or a steaming rack
st: Soak the dried ribs in cold water for 24 hours, changing the water 2 or 3 times, to remove salt.
Put a rack in the bottom of a large pot and pour in water just below the rack.
Lay the soaked ribs on the rack in a single or double layer, skin-side up.
Cover tightly and steam over medium heat for 2 to 2.5 hours until the meat pulls from the bone. Top up water when needed.
Boil the potatoes in unsalted water for 20 minutes until tender.
Boil the rutabaga in water for 25 minutes until soft, then drain.
Mash the rutabaga with the butter and [[0.5 tsp]] salt, adding a pinch of nutmeg if you like.
Check the meat is above 145°F (63°C) and fork-tender.
Serve with the mash, potatoes and some of the cooking juices.
Pour the whey, milk and cream into a wide, heavy pot.
Bring to a boil over medium-high heat, stirring now and then.
Keep it at a lively simmer for about 1.5 hours, stirring more often as the liquid reduces and darkens.
When it becomes thick and caramel-colored, lower the heat and stir constantly so it does not scorch.
Cook for 20 to 30 minutes more until it looks like thick fudge and pulls away from the pot sides.
Line a small loaf pan with parchment paper.
Beat the hot mixture with a wooden spoon for 3 minutes to smooth it, then pour into the pan and press flat.
Cool completely, then chill until firm, about 2 hours.
Slice paper-thin with a cheese slicer and serve on bread or waffles.
Beat the eggs and sugar for 2 minutes until pale.
Mix in the melted butter, cream and vanilla.
Stir in the flour and cardamom until you have a smooth batter like thick pancake batter.
Heat a krumkake iron over medium heat and grease lightly if needed.
Pour or spoon about [[1 tbsp]] of batter onto the center of the iron, close and press for 30 to 45 seconds until light golden.
Lift the hot cookie off with a spatula or thin knife.
Working fast while it is hot and flexible, roll it around a wooden cone or a rolled paper cone.
Hold for 10 seconds until set, then cool seam-side down.
Fill with whipped cream right before serving, or enjoy plain.
Mix the warm milk, yeast and a pinch of the sugar. Let stand for 5 minutes until foamy.
Add the flour, remaining sugar, cardamom, salt, egg and [[0.25 cup]] butter and knead for 8 minutes until smooth.
Cover and let rise for 1 hour until doubled.
Mix the remaining [[0.25 cup]] butter with the cinnamon and brown sugar into a paste.
Roll the dough into a large rectangle about 12 by 16 inches and spread with the paste.
Roll up from the long side and cut into 12 slices.
Place the buns cut-side up on a lined baking sheet with space between them. Let rise 30 minutes.
Heat the oven to 400°F (200°C). Bake for 12 to 15 minutes until golden.
Whisk the powdered sugar and glaze milk together and drizzle over the warm buns.
Whisk the flour, sugar, baking powder, cardamom and salt in a large bowl.
In another bowl, whisk the eggs, milk and melted butter.
Pour the wet mixture into the dry and stir until just smooth. A few small lumps are fine.
Let the batter rest for 10 minutes.
Heat a heart-shaped waffle iron and grease it lightly.
Pour in enough batter to fill the iron, about [[0.33 cup]] per heart.
Cook for 3 to 4 minutes until golden and crisp.
Keep finished waffles on a rack so they stay crisp.
Serve warm with a spoonful of sour cream and jam.
Chill a large bowl and the whisk for 15 minutes in the freezer so the cream whips faster.
Pour in the cream, powdered sugar and vanilla and whip on medium speed for 3 minutes until soft peaks form that just hold their shape.
Fold in two thirds of the cloudberry jam with a spatula, leaving marbled streaks and not a fully blended color.
Spoon the cream into six glasses and top with the remaining jam.
Chill for at least 30 minutes and serve with a krumkake or shortbread on the side.
nt: Don't cook: just whip and fold
Best swap: use raspberry or apricot jam 1 to 1 if cloudberries are not available.

st: Grind the almonds to a fine meal in a food processor and mix with [[2.5 cup]] powdered sugar.
Lightly beat 1 egg white and stir it in with the almond extract. Knead into a firm dough, adding a little more white if crumbly.
Warm the dough in a pan over low heat for 5 minutes, stirring, then cool 15 minutes. This makes it easier to roll.
Heat the oven to 350°F. Grease ring molds or shape rings by hand on parchment, rolling ropes about 0.5 inch thick.
Make 12 to 18 rings in graduated sizes, joining the ends of each rope into a circle.
Bake for 15 minutes until golden at the edges. Cool completely on the sheet before moving.
Whisk the remaining egg whites with [[0.5 cup]] powdered sugar and lemon juice into a thick icing. Pipe a zigzag onto each ring.
Stack the rings from largest to smallest into a tower.
nt: Best swap: almond flour in place of the ground whole almonds, 1 to 1.
